summary.intent: Run a principal-engineer adversarial review of Callisto (a polyglot release tool) ahead of v1, re-scope it to avoid over-engineering, then plan and start hardening first-release mechanics and initial-setup DX (easy defaults, expert config).
summary.outcome: Produced a five-lens adversarial report and a trimmed ship-first v1 plan (8 gates, soon-after list, explicit over-engineering list, legacy-removal list), plus analysis of first-publish and package-pull policies. Implemented and opened a PR making `init` default to independent versioning, write the workflow by default for GitHub origins, and print next-steps secrets, with updated tests, specs, README, publishing.md and a changeset; CI passed.

repo: Callisto ADRs: committed decision is release authority (ADR 2), no-journal recovery by observing registries/git (ADR 3/9), native tools publish and own auth (ADR 4), format-preserving writes (ADR 8), directory-keyed internal identity (ADR 11); ADR 12 still says 'Proposed' though canonical ecosystem/name ids are shipped.
Default tag template is `{display id}@{version}`, so tag names change (e.g. `foo@1.0.0` to `cargo/foo@1.1.0`) when another ecosystem adds a same-named package; a key 1.0 contract risk.

Hidden CLI commands (release plan/execute/artifact-manifest, release-pr, matrix, compose-pr-body, schema) are required by generated workflows and are effectively public API; six release documents carry different schemaVersions.
npm access comes from `publishConfig.access` in package.json, not a Callisto registry config key.
AGENTS.md forbids citing spec/criterion IDs in tests, so spec-to-test traceability tooling is structurally awkward; docs/specs/*.json hold ~244 acceptance criteria.
Integration tests that run `init --yes` in a repo with a GitHub origin now also get a workflow, so they need `--no-workflow`.
Sandbox causes unrelated test failures (uv can't write its cache); the authoritative CI run must be done outside the sandbox.
Perf gains in 0.12+ came entirely from batching; other perf hints were reverted.
Registry cache windows: npm docs up to ~5 min, PyPI index and crates.io sparse index up to ~10 min.

code.finding: release-source checkout uses persist-credentials: true, leaving a contents:write token readable by publish-time build scripts; policy script requires it and templates copy it.
Release-commit verification checks only decision file, changeset deletion, claimed manifests and changelogs; other paths (.npmrc, build.rs, callisto.toml) can change undetected.
Built-in registries with no configured URL pass no explicit --registry, so destination comes from the checkout's .npmrc/.cargo/config.toml.
actionlint/zizmor lint of the generated workflow silently skips when tools are missing, and CI does not install them.
Trust-path git batch parser claims fail-closed behavior but has no unit tests.
TOOL_SHAPES lists only gh, git, npm and cargo, so pnpm/yarn/bun publish argv is never checked against real tools.

friction: Stale /tmp PR body file caused PR #348 to be created with old text; had to detect and fix it.
Security subagent could not run git commands due to the worktree guard, so its findings are read-only, unreproduced.
Agent scratch directories collided, requiring some probes to be redone.
Nine init tests plus a subprocess dispatch test broke from the changed defaults and needed updating.
Sandbox-specific test failures (uv cache) obscured real results until CI was rerun outside the sandbox.
Required-check ruleset is not in the repo, so which CI jobs gate merges is unknown.
open_items: Decisions for user: tag naming (keep+document vs always qualify), accept/trim ADR 12, skip non-publishable members by default, reject `publish-to = nuget`, OIDC for npm, private workspace root exclusion.

v1 gates not yet implemented: unresolved changeset entry hard error, skip version-less/non-publishable members, release-commit path allow-list, explicit built-in registry URL, local-only tag diagnostic, installer main-HEAD fallback removal and --source-ref attestation, extend credential scrub list, stability page.
Legacy removal PR: delete [init] table, release.profiles, setup_git_user input, and the installer fallback.

First-release work: static metadata preflight in release --dry-run, 'first publish' shown in plan, taken-name diagnosis replacing misleading E320, 'pulling a release' runbook, error for publish-says-exists-but-not-visible.
Scripted 'first ten minutes' matrix and fresh-repo rehearsal with local registries; real-registry end-to-end run needs user credentials.

Soon-after cheap fixes: npm range parsing, peer co-release floor, 'already published' detection, E121 message, package.json inline formatting, CI timeouts, scheduled provider-contract, git_batch tests, pnpm/yarn/bun flag contract.
Verify crates.io deletion thresholds and PEP 763 status against live sources before documenting; verify registry first-publish credential claims.
Real-registry run script and stability page not started; init defaults PR opened but not yet merged.
